title: Carry a 1.8 kg school microscope to the bench mat by its arm and under its base, never by the tube, stage or knobs
instruction: Move the microscope onto the blue bench mat, standing upright with its arm toward you as it stands now, and let go of it.
context: Fetching the microscope to the bench is how every school biology practical begins, and nearly everyone was taught the rule: "Carry the scope with both hands, one on the arm, one on the base" (a college lab guide); "if picked up by stage or eyepiece holder it can become misaligned" (a microscope care guide); "never hold the stage, observation tube, or focusing knob when moving the frame" (Olympus/Evident). Here the microscope is a true-size student model, 30 cm tall and 1.8 kg (AmScope M150C: 4 lb), front-heavy, standing flat on a mat. One gripper on its arm cannot lift it: the grip turns on the arm and it tips forward onto the front of its base. The other gripper has to get under the base: it must be rocked back a little on its base's back edge so a finger can slide under the raised side, and then both lift it level, carry it and set it down square, without ever touching the tube, head, stage or knobs.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left, z up from the table top. Start mat: dark grey rubber, 24 x 16 x 0.3 cm, fixed, centre x 30.0, y 7.5. Bench mat: blue rubber, 24 x 16 x 0.3 cm, fixed, centre x 30.0, y -10.5 (2 cm gap between the mats). Microscope (loose, 1.80 kg, student monocular LED model like the AmScope M150C), standing upright on the start mat, base centred on it, its arm toward the robot: white cast-metal base 18 x 13 x 3.0 cm on four 4 mm rubber feet (1.00 kg, back edge at x 21.0); white arm 4.0 cm deep and 3.6 cm wide rising from the back of the base to 20 cm, then reaching forward over the stage to carry the head (0.32 kg); black focus knobs (38 and 24 mm) on both sides of the arm 7.5 cm up (0.06 kg); black stage 8.9 x 8.9 x 1.0 cm at 12.1-13.1 cm with two clips, a slide and the condenser under it (0.20 kg); head with a revolving nosepiece and three objectives under it and the eyepiece tube leaning 45 degrees back toward the robot, top 30.5 cm up (0.22 kg). Both arms start at the ready pose, grippers open. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Tracked every control step from PhysX contact forces between each part and every link of both arms. 0 for the rest of the run if: an arm touches the stage (with clips and condenser), the head (with nosepiece, objectives, tube and eyepiece) or a focus knob with 0.5 N or more; the microscope tilts more than 15 degrees from upright; it drops (its base falls faster than 0.4 m/s, a free fall of 8 mm); or the base's lowest corner is more than 3 cm above the table for 0.25 s without one gripper on the arm and the other on the base, each pressing 1 N or more (a one-hand carry). Otherwise 0.25 once it has been carried that way (base 3 cm or more up, held on the arm and on the base); 0.5 once it then stands upright (within 5 degrees) resting on the bench mat (lowest corner within 5 mm of the mat's top) with all four base corners over the mat and turned no more than 15 degrees from its start; 1.0 when it is also released (no arm touching it) and still (under 1 mm in 1 s) for 1 s. Doing nothing scores 0. Real trial: the touches, tilt, a drop, the hands on the arm and base while it is up, and the release are judged from the video; the mat check with a ruler and the tilt with a phone level app.
reset_notes: Stand the microscope back on the grey mat, base centred on it and its arm toward the robot, stage lowered and the 4X objective in place; check that nothing on it has moved. Simulation: each trial starts the simulator afresh.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, 20 Hz control. The microscope is boxes, cylinders and capsules at true size and mass; its parts are separate bodies on locked joints so touches can be told apart (focus, stage travel and the nosepiece do not move). A touch is a PhysX contact force of 0.5 N or more. Friction: rubber feet and mat 0.8 to 0.9 (estimates). Grip forces are simulator values.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (both grippers hovered beside and above the microscope, the left one over its head and stage, and never took hold of it; it never moved); demo: 1.0
